blogs.title: When B12 Deficiency Doesn't Tell the Whole Story: Recognizing Diagnostic Tension in Multisystem Disease
blogs.description: This post will explore the clinical reasoning behind recognizing when a seemingly straightforward diagnosis (severe B12 deficiency) fails to explain the full constellation of symptoms. We'll discuss the concept of 'diagnostic tension'—the mismatch between a proposed diagnosis and the totality of clinical findings—and how premature closure on an obvious but insufficient explanation can delay recognition of rare genetic conditions. Practical strategies for when to expand the differential and pursue genetic testing will be discussed.

blogs.title: Dyskeratosis Congenita Without the Triad: Adult Presentations of Telomere Biology Disorders
blogs.description: Classical teaching emphasizes the mucocutaneous triad (oral leukoplakia, nail dystrophy, reticular skin pigmentation) for dyskeratosis congenita, but adult presentations often lack these hallmark features. This post will review how telomere biology disorders can masquerade as 'idiopathic' pulmonary fibrosis, liver disease, or bone marrow failure in young adults, with premature greying, osteoporosis, and cytopenias serving as subtle clues. We'll discuss the expanding phenotype and why TBDs should be on the differential for any young patient with unexplained organ fibrosis.

blogs.title: PARN Mutations: Expanding the Phenotype Beyond Pulmonary Fibrosis
blogs.description: PARN variants are increasingly recognized in pulmonary fibrosis, but this case highlights hepatic fibrosis and hematologic vulnerability as part of the spectrum. This post will examine the biology of PARN (a poly(A)-specific ribonuclease), the clinical differences between monoallelic and biallelic variants, and the emerging evidence that hepatic involvement may be more common than previously appreciated. We'll discuss how this gene fits within the broader telomere maintenance pathway.

blogs.title: The Liver in Telomere Biology Disorders: An Underrecognized Target Organ
blogs.description: While pulmonary fibrosis is well-established in TBDs, hepatic fibrosis and cirrhosis are often overlooked. This post will review the emerging evidence for liver involvement in TERC, TERT, and now PARN mutation carriers, with data suggesting cirrhosis may affect up to one-third of patients. We'll discuss the mechanism (hepatocytes as rapidly dividing cells), clinical implications for screening, and why transient elastography should be considered in TBD patients.

blogs.title: Variants of Uncertain Significance: When Clinical Correlation Trumps Genetic Classification
blogs.description: This case features a VUS in PARN—a variant classified as 'uncertain' yet clinically actionable. This post will discuss the practical approach to VUS interpretation, including the role of in silico prediction tools, functional domain conservation, and most importantly, phenotype-genotype correlation. We'll explore how clinicians can work with geneticists to interpret uncertain findings and make management decisions while avoiding both over-interpretation and therapeutic nihilism.
